clauses.statement: aggregateDeliveryMetrics's agent_consumption_ms charge for a reviews[] entry whose close_reason is 'completed' equals the entry's full finished_at - started_at duration, unconditionally, even when that duration exceeds the entry's own timeout_ms.
clauses.rationale: resolveConsumptionCharge returns the raw duration as soon as close_reason === 'completed', before it ever inspects timeout_ms. The real architecture_boundary lifecycle #2 from the 2026-08-05 incident ledger (744,613ms, timeout_ms=600,000, close_reason=completed) is the concrete case this exempts: a genuinely completed review must never be shortened by the deadline bound.

clauses.statement: Given a reviews[] entry whose close_reason is timeout, replaced, manual_shutdown, or any value other than 'completed' (including an unrecognized future value), and whose timeout_ms is a finite positive number, when aggregateDeliveryMetrics computes the entry's charge, then the charge is min(finished_at - started_at, timeout_ms), the excluded remainder (duration - charge) is added to deadline_excluded_ms, and deadline_excluded_count is incremented by 1 for that entry.
clauses.rationale: Pins the bounded branch against the real gate_evidence lifecycle #10 from the 2026-08-05 incident ledger: 7,017,457ms (116.9 minutes) against timeout_ms=600,000, verified identically across all four non-completed close_reason values so the bound is proven to key off close_reason !== 'completed', not off a timeout-specific string match.

story_refs.text_snippet: close_reason が 'completed' 以外...timeout_ms が有限値の場合、計上区間は min(finished_at - started_at, timeout_ms) に縮められる

test_refs.case: DBA-S-2: timeout, replaced, manual_shutdown, and an unrecognized future close_reason are all bounded to timeout_ms

clauses.statement: Given a reviews[] entry whose timeout_ms is missing, null, NaN, a non-numeric string, zero, or negative, when aggregateDeliveryMetrics computes the entry's charge, then the charge equals the full finished_at - started_at duration regardless of close_reason, and neither deadline_excluded_ms nor deadline_excluded_count is incremented for that entry.
clauses.rationale: This is the backward-compatibility fallback: existing callers that never populate close_reason/timeout_ms on their reviews[] entries must keep today's unbounded-sum behavior exactly. resolveConsumptionCharge's Number.isFinite/positivity guard runs before Math.min, so any non-finite or non-positive timeout_ms short-circuits to the full duration.

story_refs.text_snippet: timeout_ms が欠落または非有限...の場合、close_reason に関わらず現在どおり全区間を計上する（後方互換）

clauses.statement: aggregateDeliveryMetrics's review_wait_ms and subagent_wall_clock_ms remain computed from unionDuration(intervals) exactly as before this Story, and are never reduced by the close_reason/timeout_ms deadline bound that agent_consumption_ms now applies.
clauses.rationale: boundAgentConsumption is a separate computation feeding only agent_consumption_ms/deadline_excluded_ms/deadline_excluded_count; the review_wait_ms/subagent_wall_clock_ms lines are untouched by this Story's diff. Deliberately shrinking the deadline-bound metric while leaving the wall-clock metric alone preserves the operational fact of how long the story was actually blocked, which is the point rejected alternative (a) in the architecture doc would have obscured.

clauses.statement: Both authorizeAgentReviewDispatch (src/agent-review.js) and buildDeliveryEfficiencyContext (src/pr-manager.js) construct each reviews[] entry passed into aggregateDeliveryMetrics with close_reason and timeout_ms copied verbatim from the corresponding lifecycle entry, so the deadline-bounded charge is reachable from both of this repository's live review-lifecycle call sites without any change to aggregateDeliveryMetrics's own call signature.
clauses.rationale: aggregateDeliveryMetrics has three producers upstream (including story-run-portfolio.js's mergeCostAttribution, which forwards reviews[] unchanged), but only these two sites construct reviews[] from raw lifecycle entries. Both were changed to add exactly the same two fields, keeping the bound-vs-not-bound decision logic in the single aggregateDeliveryMetrics call site instead of duplicating min(duration, timeout_ms) at each caller.

clauses.statement: aggregateDeliveryMetrics's return value includes deadline_excluded_ms (total milliseconds excluded across all bounded reviews[] entries) and deadline_excluded_count (number of entries bounded), both null exactly when agent_consumption_ms is null (incomplete review timing) and otherwise numeric; withDeadlineExclusionVisibility (src/agent-review.js) carries both fields onto the dispatch-decision budget object, and story-run-portfolio.js's emptyCostAttribution/COUNT_COST_KEYS carry deadline_excluded_ms/deadline_excluded_count through persisted portfolio cost attribution, so pr prepare's efficiency report and dispatch decision evidence do not silently drop the excluded amount.
clauses.rationale: A bound that shrinks agent_consumption_ms without a visible trail would be indistinguishable from a loosened guardrail. deadline_excluded_ms/deadline_excluded_count are threaded through every layer that persists or reports agent_consumption_ms: the aggregator return value, the dispatch-decision budget object consumed by owner-facing evidence, and the portfolio's persisted cost_attribution shape (whose emptyCostAttribution defaults and COUNT_COST_KEYS allowlist would otherwise silently drop the two new fields).

clauses.statement: Given the real 10-entry story-vibepro-content-scoped-evidence-reuse-key review lifecycle ledger observed on 2026-08-05 (architecture_boundary x4, gate_evidence x6, all timeout_ms=600000, nine entries close_reason=completed and one entry close_reason=timeout at 7,017,457ms), when aggregateDeliveryMetrics is called with that ledger as literal reviews[] input, then agent_consumption_ms equals 4,656,074 (down from an unbounded sum of 11,073,531), deadline_excluded_ms equals 6,417,457, and deadline_excluded_count equals 1 -- not 10 -- demonstrating that the design does not degenerate to count x timeout_ms.
clauses.rationale: This is the story's central non-degeneracy proof, fixed against measured production numbers rather than synthetic fixtures: 3 of the 10 real entries individually exceed the 600,000ms deadline, but bounding fires for only the 1 whose close_reason is not 'completed'. A collapse to count x timeout_ms here would reproduce the exact failure mode (a measured tier with no real producer) that stopped the earlier, unmerged story-vibepro-work-based-agent-consumption-budget design.

clauses.statement: Given a review lifecycle entry's close_reason status transitions to one of four terminal values recognized by resolveLifecycleEffectiveStatus and REVIEW_CLOSE_REASONS (completed, timeout, replaced, manual_shutdown) at the end of the agent review dispatch flow, when aggregateDeliveryMetrics processes that status transition to compute the entry's agent_consumption_ms charge, then only the three non-completed terminal status transitions are subject to the timeout_ms deadline bound, so the deadline-bounded attribution flow never shortens the completed status transition's charge.
clauses.rationale: Restates the architecture doc's flow diagram (Lifecycle -> Duration -> close_reason branch -> Bound/Full/Fallback -> Sum) in workflow state-transition terms: REVIEW_CLOSE_REASONS (src/agent-review.js) enumerates the four terminal states this Story's bound branches on, and resolveLifecycleEffectiveStatus (src/agent-review.js) is the existing state-transition logic that already treats 'elapsed_ms > timeout_ms' as a boundary condition. This clause documents that aggregateDeliveryMetrics's close_reason branch mirrors an existing state boundary rather than introducing a new one.

diagrams.rationale: Threat surface for this Story per the architecture doc 残余リスク section: the operator-supplied close_reason discriminator could mislabel a completed review as timeout to reduce its charged agent_consumption_ms. Mitigated by (1) close_evidence/result_artifact normally accompanying a completed close, making a false timeout claim an evidence-integrity violation, and (2) deadline_excluded_ms/deadline_excluded_count always surfacing in pr prepare output so large exclusions are conspicuous rather than silent.
